headline: High-risk default interaction: Devin can ingest and act on Dagster outputs via shared integrations, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no direct output channel, but Devin can ingest files, repo clones, Slack, Jira, Notion, and MCP content. If Dagster-generated artifacts are passed into Devin through those shared surfaces, Devin may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not documented directly for this pair, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are copied into a shared repo, ticket, or Slack thread that Devin reads
IF Devin parses Dagster-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Dagster outputs into Devin-facing channels
Add a provenance banner to all Dagster-generated artifacts
Require manual review before Devin acts on any Dagster text
Restrict Devin to read-only access on shared threads
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the integration boundary

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster itself shows no filesystem read/write or network egress, but Devin has broad network egress, cloud workspace files, repo clones, and multiple write-capable integrations. If Dagster data is placed in shared workspace files or tickets, Devin can transmit that context to third-party services or external APIs. The pairwise leakage path is indirect but credible from the profiles.
conditions: IF Dagster artifacts contain sensitive data and are stored in Devin-accessible workspace files
IF Devin forwards those artifacts through GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, or MCP integrations
mitigations: Keep sensitive Dagster outputs out of shared workspaces
Limit Devin integrations to the minimum required set
Redact secrets before exporting Dagster artifacts
Turn off automatic sync from Dagster outputs to tickets or chat
requires-engineering: enforce per-dataset access controls and DLP at the workspace boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster is non-runnable and has no write or network capabilities, while Devin can write files, modify git state, and use MCP. There is no direct write-write conflict from Dagster alone, but if Dagster orchestrates artifacts that Devin edits in the same repo or workspace, overlapping mutable-resource access exists. Because the shared mutable surface is plausible but not explicit, severity stays medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository or cloud workspace
IF Devin edits files that Dagster also generates or refreshes
mitigations: Assign separate directories for Dagster and Devin outputs
Freeze Dagster-generated files before Devin edits them
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Require lockfiles or lease tokens for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor with browser, shell, and write-capable integrations, so if it consumes Dagster-produced outputs as authoritative, it can turn a mistaken upstream artifact into downstream commits, tickets, or messages. Dagster does not verify Devin's actions, and the pair lacks a documented verification gate, making the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF Devin uses Dagster output as the source of truth for code, tickets, or chat messages
IF no human or automated verification step checks Dagster output before Devin acts
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin acts on Dagster outputs
Add a validation step between Dagster and Devin
Limit Devin to draft-only actions on shared artifacts
Log and diff all Dagster-derived inputs before execution
requires-engineering: implement schema validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and shows no handled secrets or data classes, while Devin is closed-source, cloud-hosted, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens across GitHub, Slack, Jira, and Notion. If regulated or sensitive data flows from Dagster-managed pipelines into Devin's cloud workspace, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF Dagster-managed data includes regulated records or secrets
IF those records are processed in Devin's cloud workspace or third-party integrations
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to Devin
Block regulated datasets from Devin integrations
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings
Use pseudonymized copies for Devin tasks
requires-engineering: enforce residency and retention policy controls per data class
